The safe mode added to `promptfoo eval` in version 0.125.0 turns off inline JavaScript assertions and shared transforms. It is activated using the command line option `--safe-mode`, the environment variable `PROMPTFOO_SAFE_MODE=true`, or by setting `commandLineOptions.safeMode: true` in the eval configuration. This mode rejects string-based JavaScript assertions and inline expressions handled by the shared transform helper.

The relevant information is stated as follows:

- "Use `promptfoo eval --safe-mode` or `PROMPTFOO_SAFE_MODE=true` to reject string-based JavaScript assertions and inline expressions handled by the shared transform helper." [2] promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md (lines 11-64)

- "Config settings cannot disable a guard enabled by the CLI flag or process environment." [2] promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md (lines 11-64)

This indicates that when safe mode is enabled, these specific JavaScript features are turned off. However, it is important to note that this mode is not a complete sandbox and does not make untrusted configurations entirely safe to run. [2] promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md (lines 11-64)
